note: The Genesis series' Commons and Rares are made from these (scripts/gnomes.ts): an archetype is a look that belongs together; a palette is a set of colours that do, its key colour (the hat's, a baker's coat) worn with any of the archetype's wardrobe for the other; a Common is an archetype in one of its palettes with a beard and a few of its things, a Rare one more (a pattern or a piece) and a trail. Lines are an opener (the palette's, or a Rare's piece or pattern) and the archetype's tail; both stand alone, so any pair reads. Colours are data/../vocab.ts COLOURS names.

scarf: The scarf is three seasons long.
Knitted the scarf, then kept going.
Never takes the scarf off, even indoors.
bowtie: The bow tie is for special occasions. Every hole is one.
Dressed for a wedding, playing golf.
Ties the bow tie twice before a big putt.
plume: The feather was a gift from a very tall bird.
A plume that waves at every crowd.
earmuffs: Earmuffs on: no advice gets through.
The earmuffs block out the heckling.
satchel: The satchel holds three balls and a sandwich.
Packs for every hole as if it were a trip.
Nobody knows what is in the satchel.
medal: The medal is for something. Nobody remembers what.
Wears the medal on the green, for luck.
Won the medal at a hole nobody else finished.

stripes: Wears the stripes sideways, to look wider.
spots: Spotted all over, like a happy toadstool.
checks: The checks were a tablecloth once.
zigzag: A zigzag coat, which explains the putting.
The zigzag is how the ball went last time.
argyle: Argyle, as a golfer should be.
The diamonds are knitted, not real.
patchwork: Patched with every hole's worn-out flag.

palettes.name: Tomato
lines: The hat ripened first.
Tomato-red, from the kitchen garden.

palettes.name: Lavender
lines: Lavender hat, lavender mood.
Smells faintly of the lavender border.

palettes.name: Marigold
lines: A marigold hat keeps the aphids off.
Orange as a marigold, twice as stubborn.

palettes.name: Radish
lines: Radish-pink on top, crisp underneath.
Pulled up with the radishes, kept.

palettes.name: Cornflower
lines: Cornflower blue, picked this morning.
The blue hat was a seed packet once.

palettes.name: Plum Tree
lines: Plum hat, from the tree by hole 9.
Ripe as a plum in August.

palettes.name: Pumpkin
lines: Grows prize pumpkins. Wears one, nearly.
The hat is the colour of the October patch.

palettes.name: Sunflower
lines: Turns to face the sun, then the flag.
Sunflower yellow, turned to the green.
Weeds the rough between putts.
Talks to the hedges. They listen.
Has never met a divot that could not be replanted.
Waters the fairway whatever the forecast.
Calls the bunkers flowerbeds that have not happened yet.
Prunes the flagstick when nobody is looking.
Knows every blade of grass by its first name.
Composts bad putts. They come back as good ones.
Measures every putt in seed rows.
Says the green is greener on this side.
Plants a bulb at every hole-in-one.
Keeps the slugs off the greens by asking nicely.
Rakes the bunker before and after, just in case.
Would rather mow the hole than play it.
Reads the green like a seed catalogue.
Has a name for every worm on the course.
Carries a trowel in case the cup needs moving.
Grew up in a window box. Has been climbing since.

palettes.name: Reed
lines: Reed-green hat, for hiding on the bank.
The hat blends in with the reeds. The gnome does not.

palettes.name: Pondside
lines: A pond-teal hat, wet at the brim.
Teal as still water at dawn.

palettes.name: Trout
lines: Speckled like a trout, nearly.
A trout-grey hat with a pink lining.

palettes.name: Kingfisher
lines: Kingfisher blue, kingfisher patience.
Blue as a kingfisher, and nearly as quick.

palettes.name: Float
lines: A float-red hat, so the others know where to look.
Red on top, like a float that has not bobbed.

palettes.name: Mudbank
lines: A hat the colour of a good mudbank.
Mud-brown hat, spotless gnome.

palettes.name: Dawn
lines: Up before the fish, in a dawn-pink hat.
Coral hat, first light, first cast.

palettes.name: Lily
lines: A lily-pad hat. The frogs have opinions.
Sits on lily pads. They mostly hold.
Fishes the water hazards. Has caught eleven balls.
Waits for the putt like a bite.
Says the one that got away was a birdie.
Casts a line across every pond, out of habit.
Never hurries. The fish never do.
Measures putts in rod lengths.
Has a lucky fly in the hat and a lucky ball in the pond.
Takes a flask, a chair and four hours a hole.
Lands the putt, then lets it go.
Knows where the frogs sit and putts round them.
Swears the ball was this big.
Reads the ripples before the green.
Brings a net to the water hazard, as a precaution.
Hums to the carp between strokes.
Calls a three-putt a good day on the bank.
Ties knots in the flag cord when bored.
Keeps maggots in the hat. Does not say so.
Has never fallen in. Officially.

palettes.name: Navy
lines: Whites on, ready for inspection.
A cap so white it squints back.

palettes.name: Harbour
lines: Harbour whites, pressed for the dance.
Dressed for shore leave.

palettes.name: Signal
lines: A signal-red cap: man the putter.
Red cap, so the lookout can find it.

palettes.name: Deep Blue
lines: Navy cap, a sea of patience under it.
Deep blue on top, calm underneath.

palettes.name: Lagoon
lines: A lagoon-blue cap, salt in its seams.
The cap came back from the lagoon bluer.

palettes.name: Buoy
lines: Bright as a buoy, and as easy to spot.
An orange cap: man overboard, found.

palettes.name: Galley
lines: A galley-yellow cap with a soup stain.
Mustard cap, smells of the galley.

palettes.name: Spray
lines: Sea-spray green, dried in the sun.
The cap went seafoam after one storm.
Calls the cup the harbour.
Steers by the flag and the stars.
Reads the green like a tide table.
Ties a knot in the flag cord, for luck.
Salutes the hole before every putt.
Swabs the green with a sleeve.
Was told to swab the deck. Found the golf course instead.
Swears the ball listed to port.
Rings a bell when the ball goes in.
Has a girl in every port, and a putter in every bag.
Measures putts in fathoms.
Shouts 'land ho' at every green.
Says a three-putt is choppy water.
Whistles sea shanties on the backswing.
Never putts into the wind. Waits for it to turn.
Folds the scorecard into a paper boat.
Sails round the bunkers, never through.
Has crossed every water hazard by putter.

palettes.name: Scarlet
lines: A scarlet bandana, spotted with sea salt.
Red bandana, tied tight for weather.

palettes.name: Bosun
lines: A bosun-blue bandana.
Navy cloth over a sunburnt head.

palettes.name: Coral Reef
lines: A coral bandana from the reef market.
Coral cloth from the shallow water.

palettes.name: Galleon
lines: A plum bandana from a plundered trunk.
Plum cloth, gold spots, no questions.

palettes.name: Palm
lines: Palm-green bandana, coconut-scented.
Green as the island, wrapped tight.

palettes.name: Sunset
lines: A sunset bandana, tied at dusk.
Orange cloth, the island's evening.

palettes.name: Rigging
lines: Tar-brown bandana, rope-burn hands.
The bandana smells of rigging.

palettes.name: Lagoon
lines: A lagoon bandana, still dripping.
Teal cloth, warm water.
Climbs the flagstick to see the green.
Swabs the green before every putt.
Sleeps in a hammock between holes.
Has walked the plank twice. Swims well.
Swears at the wind in three languages.
Ties every knot known, and two invented.
Keeps a biscuit in the bandana for later.
Calls the cup the hold.
Has been seasick on a putting green.
Hauls the ball out of the cup like an anchor.
Never met a rope that stayed untied.
Coils the flag cord without thinking.
Takes orders from nobody, then follows them.
Whistles for the wind, and sometimes gets it.
Puts a coin under the ball for luck.
Has a tattoo of a hole-in-one. Not a real one.
Can hold a putter in a gale.
Keeps one eye on the ball and one on the weather.

palettes.name: Strawberry
lines: Strawberry coat, jam at the cuffs.
Smells of jam tarts.

palettes.name: Blueberry
lines: Blueberry coat, flour to the elbows.
A muffin's colours, worn proudly.

palettes.name: Pistachio
lines: Pistachio coat, from the macaron shelf.
Green as a pistachio, soft as a sponge.

palettes.name: Lemon Curd
lines: Lemon coat, sharp as the curd.
A lemon tart of a gnome.

palettes.name: Toffee
lines: Toffee coat, sticky in summer.
Caramel-brown, from the toffee pan.

palettes.name: Peach Melba
lines: A peach melba coat, raspberry neckerchief.
Peach coat, ready by noon.

palettes.name: Sugared Almond
lines: Sugared-almond colours, all of them.
Pastel from the hat down.

palettes.name: Blackcurrant
lines: Blackcurrant coat, purple fingers.
The lilac coat is a crumble stain.
Bakes a cake for every birdie. It is a lot of cake.
Proves the dough while waiting for the green.
Knows the course by its smells.
Says a good putt, like a good loaf, needs rest.
Kneads the putter grip before every stroke.
Brings warm buns to the first tee.
Times every putt like a soufflé.
Measures putts in rolling pins.
Has never burnt a bun, or missed a two-footer. Allegedly.
Leaves crumbs to find the way back.
Ices the flag on special days.
Plays fast: the bread is in the oven.
Reads the green like a recipe.
Says the bunker is just very big brown sugar.
Hums while the dough rises and the ball rolls.
Keeps a spoon behind the ear, in case.
Weighs every ball before teeing off.
Has a rival at the other bakery. Also a gnome.

palettes.name: Vermilion
lines: A vermilion beret, tipped just so.
Red beret, like the masters.

palettes.name: Ultramarine
lines: Ultramarine beret, expensive pigment.
A blue beret and big ideas.

palettes.name: Ochre
lines: An ochre beret, earth from the hill.
Earth-yellow beret, still drying.

palettes.name: Charcoal
lines: A charcoal beret, for sketching.
Black beret, no compromise.

palettes.name: Viridian
lines: A viridian beret, mixed by hand.
Green beret, bold choices.

palettes.name: Magenta
lines: A magenta beret with paint on it.
The beret was a happy accident.

palettes.name: Sepia
lines: A sepia beret, old-photograph brown.
Brown beret, a sepia mood.

palettes.name: Cerulean
lines: A cerulean beret, the colour of afternoons.
Sky-blue beret for plein air.
Sketches the green before every putt.
Sees the line in colours nobody else sees.
Signs the scorecard in the corner, small.
Calls a three-putt an abstract.
Paints the flag a new colour every Sunday.
Squints at the hole with a thumb out.
Has a blue period. It is mostly bunkers.
Holds the putter like a brush, and it works.
Never finishes a round, only abandons it.
Mixes the perfect green, then putts across it.
Wears the smock to every hole, paint and all.
Says the light at hole 6 is everything.
Frames the good scorecards. There are two.
Leaves a dab of paint on every ball.
Plays in perspective: the far holes look easier.
Has painted the clubhouse from every angle.
Is between masterpieces, and between pars.
Cries at sunsets and missed putts equally.

palettes.name: Piste
lines: A red beanie for the red run.
Red bobble, white slopes.

palettes.name: Glacier
lines: A glacier-blue beanie, frost on the bobble.
Blue knit, cold nose.

palettes.name: Chalet
lines: A chalet-red beanie by the fire.
Knitted by the stove in the chalet.

palettes.name: Pine
lines: A pine-green beanie from the tree line.
Green knit, smells of pine needles.

palettes.name: Apres
lines: A berry beanie for après-golf.
Pink knit, cocoa breath.

palettes.name: Snowplough
lines: A snowplough-yellow beanie, impossible to lose.
Yellow knit, seen from the lift.

palettes.name: Alpenglow
lines: Alpenglow pink, the last light on the peak.
The beanie catches the evening light.

palettes.name: Blizzard
lines: A blizzard-grey beanie, warmer than it looks.
Grey knit, built for whiteouts.
Putts in a tuck position.
Takes every green as a black run.
Has never stopped in time on a downhill putt.
Says the bunker is just warm snow.
Waxes the ball before the first tee.
Does a little jump on every slope.
Shouts 'track!' before every putt.
Would rather take the chairlift to the green.
Knows a mogul when it sees one.
Snowploughs to a stop beside the cup.
Leans into the curve, every time.
Wipes the goggles, misses anyway.
Has been to the Alps. Talks about it.
Was first on the slopes and first on the green.
Thinks every green should have a lift.
Rolls downhill faster than the ball.
Carves a perfect line, then three-putts.
Says the cocoa tastes better after a birdie.

palettes.name: Loden
lines: A loden hat, felted in the valley.
Green felt, a red band, a long climb.

palettes.name: Edelweiss
lines: A slate-grey hat with a sprig of summer.
Grey felt, a yellow band, a long way up.

palettes.name: Valley
lines: A chestnut hat from the valley fair.
Brown felt, a cowbell's patience.

palettes.name: Gentian
lines: Gentian blue, the flower of the high pass.
A blue hat for the blue flowers.

palettes.name: Larch
lines: A larch-green hat, gold in autumn.
Olive felt, dusty boots.

palettes.name: Cowbell
lines: A cowbell-red hat; you hear him coming.
Red felt, loud boots.

palettes.name: Scree
lines: Scree-grey hat, hard-wearing.
Grey as the scree slope, and as steady.

palettes.name: Summer Pasture
lines: A pasture-green hat with a flower in the band.
Green as the high meadow in June.
Ropes up before every uphill putt.
Treats the green as a summit.
Yodels when the ball drops.
Has climbed every flagstick on the course.
Plans a route to the cup, with a bivouac.
Says the air is thinner on the 18th.
Never putts downhill without a belay.
Carries the kit of three gnomes and the patience of four.
Reads the slope by the snowmelt.
Plants a tiny flag on every green reached.
Calls the rough the approach.
Respects the mountain. And the bunker.
Has a cowbell for every par.
Stops halfway up the fairway for cheese.
Takes the long way round, on purpose.
Measures every putt in rope lengths.
Went up the mountain for the view. Stayed for the golf.
Keeps a compass, a whistle and a spare ball.

palettes.name: Signal Red
lines: A red helmet, seen down any shaft.
Signal red, for the deep galleries.

palettes.name: Copper Seam
lines: A copper-coloured helmet from the copper seam.
The helmet went orange in the copper vein.

palettes.name: Slate
lines: A slate helmet, dented twice.
Grey as the slate face it was dented on.

palettes.name: Safety
lines: A white helmet: a shift boss, almost.
White helmet, clean for once.

palettes.name: Amethyst
lines: A helmet painted after the amethyst find.
Purple helmet, lucky ever since.

palettes.name: Pit Pony
lines: A pit-pony brown helmet.
Brown helmet, tough as an old pony.

palettes.name: Moss Gallery
lines: A moss-green helmet from the damp gallery.
Moss grows on this helmet. It is fine.

palettes.name: Tin
lines: A tin helmet that rings when knocked.
Steel grey, sounds like a bell.
Taps the green with a pick to check it is solid.
Has never seen a hole he did not want to dig deeper.
Calls the cup a shaft.
Putts by feel. Down there, there was no light.
Knows a seam when he sees one; a line too.
Says the rough is softer than granite.
Has been underground so long the sun is a rumour.
Whistles to the canaries between holes.
Measures putts in pick handles.
Swears the ball went down the wrong tunnel.
Brings a sandwich in a tin, and a ball in another.
Hears the ball drop from three holes away.
Never trusts a green without supports.
Has a pick for every kind of rock and a putter for every green.
Comes up for air and a round of golf.
Polishes every pebble found on the fairway.
Calls a bunker an open-cast pit.
Keeps the score in chalk on a rock.

palettes.name: Dust
lines: A dusty hat, slapped clean once a year.
The hat is the colour of the trail.

palettes.name: Creek
lines: A creek-green hat, soaked at the brim.
Teal hat from panning the creek.

palettes.name: Claim
lines: A brick-red hat to mark the claim.
Red hat, staked out.

palettes.name: Mule
lines: A mule-brown hat, the mule's choice.
Brown hat, stubborn mule.

palettes.name: Nugget
lines: A nugget-gold hat. Not real gold. Yet.
Gold-ish hat, hopes higher.

palettes.name: Campfire
lines: A hat that smells of the campfire.
Rust-red hat, smoked at the brim.

palettes.name: Silver Strike
lines: A silver hat for the silver strike.
Silver felt; the strike was copper.

palettes.name: Canyon
lines: A canyon-orange hat, sun-faded.
Terracotta hat, canyon-baked.
Pans every water hazard for gold.
Stakes a claim on the green.
Has struck gold twice. It was brass.
Bites every ball to check it.
Talks to the mule about the line.
Says there's gold in them there bunkers.
Shakes the cup in case something is in it.
Has a map to a lost hole. It is hole 7.
Measures putts in shovel lengths.
Never leaves a green without a sample.
Swears the mule can read a putt.
Keeps a nugget in one pocket and a tee in the other.
Rolls the ball like a lucky stone.
Has a hunch about the next hole.
Weighs the scorecard as if it were dust.
Was rich for a day once. Bought a putter.
Sleeps under the stars and putts under the sun.
Knows the creek better than the course.

palettes.name: Khaki
lines: A khaki helmet, faded on the crater rim.
Khaki on top, curious underneath.

palettes.name: Ash Cloud
lines: A white helmet, grey with ash by noon.
White helmet, greyer every hole.

palettes.name: Basalt
lines: A basalt-black helmet, warm to the touch.
Black helmet, sunny disposition.

palettes.name: Jungle
lines: A jungle-green helmet from the volcano's foot.
Olive helmet, cleared a path to the green.

palettes.name: Sulphur
lines: A sulphur-yellow helmet. It smells, a bit.
Yellow as the vents.

palettes.name: Expedition
lines: An expedition helmet, mapped and stamped.
Orange helmet, seen from base camp.

palettes.name: Pumice
lines: A pumice-pale helmet, light as air.
Pale helmet. Floats.

palettes.name: Fern Gully
lines: A fern-green helmet from the gully.
Green helmet, steamy day.
Has mapped every hole, and names them after himself.
Plants a flag on every green. There is already one.
Takes notes on the cup's depth.
Says the volcano is mostly asleep.
Packs for a month to play nine holes.
Measures the slope with a sextant.
Has been lost on the fairway twice. Found both times.
Brings tea to the crater rim.
Reads the green by the steam rising off it.
Swears there is an undiscovered hole beyond the 18th.
Records every putt in a leather journal.
Has a medal from a society nobody has heard of.
Calls a birdie a discovery.
Wades through the rough with a machete. Metaphorically.
Has seen the lava up close. Kept the eyebrows.
Insists on a guide for the bunkers.
Toasts every par with warm lemonade.
Is always one hill from the edge of the map.

palettes.name: Leather
lines: A leather cap, scorched at the peak.
Brown leather, singed and proud.

palettes.name: Forge
lines: A forge-red cap.
Red cap, red cheeks, red-hot iron.

palettes.name: Anvil
lines: An anvil-grey cap. It rings, too.
Grey cap, heavy hands.

palettes.name: Quench
lines: A quench-tub teal cap.
Teal cap, steam in the beard.

palettes.name: Ember
lines: An ember-orange cap, glowing a bit.
Rust cap, still warm.

palettes.name: Bellows
lines: An olive cap from the bellows corner.
Olive cap, puffing cheeks.

palettes.name: Charcoal
lines: A charcoal cap, soot on soot.
Black cap, sparks everywhere.

palettes.name: Bronze Age
lines: A bronze cap, ancient style.
Bronze-brown cap, very old trade.
Forges a new putter every morning.
Hammers the ball straight when nobody watches.
Says the green is just a cold anvil.
Quenches the putter after every birdie.
Has burnt three gloves and no putts.
Strikes while the iron is hot, and the green is fast.
Can tell a good ball by the sound.
Measures putts in tong lengths.
Shapes every putt like a horseshoe.
Has never met a metal it could not bend. Golf, maybe.
Sweeps the sparks off the green.
Keeps the forge lit between holes.
Rivets the flag back when it bends.
Says a putt needs the right temper.
Works the bellows, then the putter.
Rings the anvil when the ball drops.
Brought a hammer to the first tee. Was asked to leave it.
Sweats more on the green than at the forge.

palettes.name: Oilskin
lines: A yellow oilskin hat, stiff with rain.
Yellow sou'wester: bring it on.

palettes.name: Gale
lines: A gale-grey hat, tied on twice.
Grey hat, holding fast.

palettes.name: Drizzle
lines: A drizzle-blue hat, damp all year.
Blue hat, soft rain.

palettes.name: Lighthouse
lines: A lighthouse-red hat.
Red hat in the fog, easy to find.

palettes.name: Thunder
lines: A thundercloud-plum hat.
Plum hat, lightning not far behind.

palettes.name: Sea Fret
lines: A sea-fret green hat, misty at the brim.
Pale green hat for grey mornings.

palettes.name: Squall
lines: A squall-navy hat, battened down.
Navy hat, dark sky.

palettes.name: Rainbow
lines: A coral hat for after the rain.
Coral, the rainbow's best bit.
Taps the barometer before every putt.
Plays only when it is raining.
Says the wind is just the green breathing.
Counts the seconds between thunder and putt.
Has a word for every kind of rain.
Licks a finger, holds it up, misses anyway.
Reads the clouds better than the green.
Putts between gusts.
Has been struck by lightning. Hair still standing.
Calls a calm day suspicious.
Ties the flag down before teeing off.
Keeps a log of every storm and every bogey.
Says the puddles are part of the course.
Splashes on purpose.
Forecasts a birdie. Usually wrong.
Never carries an umbrella; it would blow away.
Smells the storm before the first tee.
Leans into the weather, and the putt.

palettes.name: Twilight
lines: A twilight hat, a size too big.
Lilac hat, borrowed from the master.

palettes.name: Midnight
lines: A midnight hat with the moon on it.
Navy hat, studied by candlelight.

palettes.name: Potion
lines: A potion-green hat. It used to be blue.
Green hat, after the experiment.

palettes.name: Comet
lines: A comet-pink hat, still smoking.
Coral hat, singed at the tip.

palettes.name: Spellbound
lines: A berry hat, enchanted. Slightly.
Pink hat with a spell on it. Not a strong one.

palettes.name: Starless
lines: A plain grey hat: no stars yet.
Grey hat; the stars come later.

palettes.name: Moonstone
lines: A moonstone-blue hat.
Blue hat, silver moon, homework due.

palettes.name: Dragonfire
lines: A dragonfire-red hat. Small dragon.
Red hat, smells of toast.
Tried to magic the ball in. It went sideways.
Has read half the book on putting spells.
Mutters at the ball. The ball ignores it.
Turned the flag into a newt once. Turned it back.
Says the cup moved. It did not.
Practises levitation on the green. Not allowed.
Will have stars on the hat one day.
Waves a twig at the ball before every stroke.
Studies the green like a spellbook.
Knows three spells and none of them golf.
Once made it rain on the wrong hole.
Takes notes for the master on every putt.
Says the bunker is cursed. Has proof.
Sweeps the green with a broom, for practice.
Keeps a frog in the hat. Not on purpose.
Has a wand, a hat, and a three-putt.
Thinks par is a spell.
Is one good putt from a promotion.
